item_name: CONSTANT AIRSPEED - CONSTANT RATE CLIMBS / DESCENTS AND VERTICAL "S"

observations.text: SP flew the climbs and descents at constant airspeed to the level expected at this point of the syllabus, with the IP directing the pitch and power changes and executing part of the level-off. Airspeed excursions exceeded 20 knots on both entries and were arrested by the IP on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent setting of pitch and power for the constant airspeed climb is expected to improve.

SP entered and flew the climbs and descents at constant airspeed after the IP's verbal reminder of the pitch and power targets, without any IP intervention on the controls. Airspeed excursions reached 20 knots and one level-off was completed 300 feet from the assigned altitude, recognized and corrected with delay but by the SP alone. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set pitch and power for the briefed climb and descent airspeed and kept the instrument cross-check running without prompting. Errors were confined to 15 knots on airspeed and 220 feet at level-off, all recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. Control inputs were smooth and continuous, with no extreme or continuous attitude changes, and airspeed was held within 8 knots and altitude within 100 feet at each level-off. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed with exceptional accuracy, anticipating each level-off lead point and trimming off control pressures throughout. Deviations in airspeed, altitude and heading were negligible and no correction was required from the IP at any stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a pitch-first technique in which power was set only after the attitude change, did not establish the pitch and power combination required for the constant airspeed climb. Airspeed decayed 30 knots below the target and the A/C climbed through the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP took the controls to re-establish the profile. Further practice of the entry sequence for constant airspeed climbs is required.

SP completed the climbs and descents at constant airspeed to the standard required for this section, but each entry was flown only after the IP's verbal reminder of the target airspeed. Airspeed reached the 20-knot limit twice and was returned to the target with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recognition and correction of the airspeed trend without prompting is expected to improve.

SP established pitch, power and trim for the constant airspeed climbs and descents without any verbal prompting from the IP. Errors were limited to 12 knots on airspeed and 180 feet at level-off, each recognized on the cross-check and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knows and executes climbs and descents at constant airspeed as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. Airspeed was held within 7 knots throughout, heading within 4 degrees, and every level-off was completed within 100 feet of the assigned altitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the constant airspeed climbs and descents with exceptional accuracy and an uninterrupted instrument cross-check, correcting trends before they became measurable deviations. Airspeed, altitude and heading excursions were negligible and A/C control remained smooth and continuous, with no extreme attitude changes. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a degraded basic instrument scan after prolonged automated navigation, did not maintain the instrument cross-check during the constant airspeed descent and did not detect the developing pitch increase. Airspeed diverged 30 knots from the briefed value and the A/C descended 400 feet through the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the profile. Renewed practice of raw-data manual instrument flying is required.

SP, due to coarse and repeated pitch inputs instead of a small correction held against the trim, did not stabilize the pitch attitude for the constant airspeed climb, inducing continuous A/C attitude changes. Airspeed oscillated to the 20-knot limit and the level-off was completed 300 feet above the assigned altitude. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal indications.

SP executed the climbs and descents at constant airspeed within the desired standards, with pitch, power and trim set without the IP's intervention. Airspeed twice reached 15 knots from the target and one level-off was completed 200 feet high, each corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter anticipation of the level-off lead point is expected to improve.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed without mistakes and without the IP's intervention, with a continuous instrument cross-check and smooth, continuous control inputs. Airspeed was maintained within 6 knots, altitude within 90 feet at level-off and heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the constant airspeed climbs and descents with exceptional accuracy, setting the pitch and power combination at the entry and trimming so that no sustained control pressure was carried. Deviations in airspeed, altitude, heading and bank were negligible, and the transitions between climb, level flight and descent produced no extreme or continuous attitude changes. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not fly the constant airspeed climb as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and left the pitch attitude unmonitored. Airspeed diverged 25 knots from the target and the A/C climbed 350 feet through the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and set the power himself. Shedding of secondary tasks when workload increases is required.

SP, due to a level-off lead point taken at the assigned altitude instead of ahead of it, did not arrest the climb in time and did not reduce the pitch attitude progressively. The A/C overshot the assigned altitude by 300 feet and airspeed reached 20 knots above the target during the recovery. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal indications.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, interrupted the instrument cross-check while establishing the constant airspeed descent. Airspeed increased 14 knots above the target and heading drifted 8 degrees before the scan was re-established. Both errors were minor, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed accurately, promptly and without the IP's intervention. Airspeed was held within 9 knots and the level-offs within 140 feet of the assigned altitude, values that remain inside the desired standards but at their upper edge. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a finer pitch and trim technique is expected to reduce these residual deviations.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed with exceptional accuracy, holding airspeed, altitude, heading and bank with deviations that were negligible throughout the sortie. A/C control was smooth and continuous, entries and level-offs were anticipated, and the instrument cross-check was never interrupted. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the constant rate climbs and descents to the level expected at this point of the syllabus, with the IP calling the target vertical velocity and adjusting the power for the SP. The rate diverged more than 300 feet per minute from the briefed value on each entry and the level-offs were completed with the IP on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent control of vertical velocity with pitch and of airspeed with power is expected to improve.

SP established and maintained the briefed vertical velocity after the IP's verbal reminder of the pitch and power targets, without any intervention on the controls. Rate deviations reached 300 feet per minute and airspeed reached 20 knots from the target, recognized and corrected with delay but by the SP alone. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set the pitch attitude for the briefed rate and the power for the briefed airspeed without prompting, keeping the vertical velocity indicator in the cross-check. Errors did not exceed 220 feet per minute on rate and 14 knots on airspeed, and all were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executes climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. Vertical velocity was held within 100 feet per minute, airspeed within 8 knots, and each level-off was completed within 100 feet of the assigned altitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the constant rate climbs and descents with exceptional accuracy, controlling vertical velocity with pitch and airspeed with power and re-trimming after every change. Deviations in rate, airspeed and altitude were negligible and the lead point for each level-off was taken without any reminder. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to the use of power rather than pitch to control the vertical velocity, did not establish the briefed constant rate descent and allowed rate and airspeed to diverge together. The rate diverged 450 feet per minute from the briefed value and airspeed 25 knots from the target, with the result that the IP took the controls to re-establish the descent. Further practice of the pitch-for-rate and power-for-airspeed relationship is required.

SP completed the constant rate climbs and descents to the standard required for this section, but the target vertical velocity was set on each entry only after the IP's verbal reminder. The rate reached 300 feet per minute from the briefed value before the SP reacted, and the correction was applied with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - unprompted recognition of the rate trend on the vertical velocity indicator is expected to improve.

SP established the briefed rate and airspeed on each entry without any verbal prompting from the IP, using small pitch corrections held against the trim. Errors were limited to 200 feet per minute on rate and 12 knots on airspeed, each recognized on the cross-check and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate accurately, promptly and with full competence, without the IP's intervention. Vertical velocity was maintained within 120 feet per minute, airspeed within 7 knots and heading within 4 degrees throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the constant rate climbs and descents with exceptional accuracy, anticipating each level-off and adjusting pitch in increments small enough that the vertical velocity indicator never oscillated. Rate, airspeed and altitude deviations were negligible and A/C control remained smooth and continuous throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to absorption in a cockpit indication that left the descent rate unmonitored, did not maintain the briefed constant rate descent and did not cross-check the altimeter against the vertical velocity indicator. The rate diverged 500 feet per minute from the briefed value and the A/C descended 400 feet through the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP directed the level-off and corrected the power setting. Continuing to fly the aircraft while a single indication is being assessed is required.

SP, due to chasing the vertical velocity indicator with large pitch inputs, did not hold a stabilized attitude for the constant rate climb and induced continuous A/C attitude changes. Rate excursions reached 300 feet per minute and airspeed reached 20 knots from the target. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal indications.

SP executed the climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate within the desired standards, without the IP's intervention. Vertical velocity twice reached 230 feet per minute from the briefed value and airspeed 13 knots from the target, each corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - steadier pitch control between the rate and airspeed corrections is expected to improve.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate without mistakes and without the IP's intervention, with smooth and continuous control inputs. Vertical velocity was held within 110 feet per minute, airspeed within 6 knots and each level-off within 90 feet of the assigned altitude. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the constant rate climbs and descents with exceptional accuracy, setting the attitude for the briefed rate at the entry and trimming so that the rate required no further correction. Deviations in rate, airspeed, altitude and heading were negligible, and the transitions between climb, level flight and descent were made without any extreme attitude change. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments, did not fly the constant rate descent as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not detect the increasing vertical velocity. The rate diverged 450 feet per minute from the briefed value and airspeed 28 knots from the target, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls and re-established the descent. Renewed emphasis on a continuous instrument cross-check is required.

SP, due to a level-off lead point that did not account for the briefed rate of descent, did not begin the pitch change in time and did not reduce the vertical velocity progressively. The A/C descended 300 feet below the assigned altitude and airspeed reached 20 knots above the target during the recovery. Both deviations were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal indications.

SP, due to complacency on a maneuver flown repeatedly without incident, did not verify the vertical velocity against the briefed value after each power change in the constant rate climb. The rate drifted 210 feet per minute from the target and airspeed 12 knots before the deviation was noticed. Both errors were minor, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate accurately, promptly and without the IP's intervention. Vertical velocity remained within 140 feet per minute and airspeed within 9 knots, values inside the desired standards but at their upper edge, and two corrections were needed on the descent. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a finer pitch and trim technique is expected to reduce these residual deviations.

SP executed climbs and descents at constant airspeed and rate with exceptional accuracy, holding rate, airspeed, altitude and heading with deviations that were negligible throughout. A/C control was smooth and continuous, every level-off was anticipated and the instrument cross-check was never interrupted. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" to the level expected at this point of the syllabus, with the IP calling each reversal point and setting the power. The rate diverged more than 300 feet per minute from the briefed value and the reversals were made more than 300 feet from the assigned altitudes, with the IP taking the controls on the second cycle. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent timing of the reversal and unprompted control of the rate are expected to improve.

SP flew consecutive Vertical "S" cycles after the IP's verbal reminder of the reversal altitude, without any intervention on the controls. Rate deviations reached 300 feet per minute and the reversals were made 300 feet from the assigned altitude, recognized and corrected with delay but by the SP alone. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" with each reversal initiated on the SP's own cross-check of altimeter and vertical velocity indicator, without prompting. Errors did not exceed 220 feet per minute on rate, 200 feet at the reversal and 8 degrees of bank, all recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executes the Vertical "S" as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. The rate was held within 100 feet per minute, the reversals were made within 100 feet of the assigned altitudes, bank within 4 degrees and airspeed within 8 knots. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" with exceptional accuracy, anticipating every reversal and coordinating the pitch change with the bank so that no cycle required a secondary correction. Deviations in rate, altitude, bank and heading were negligible and A/C control was smooth and continuous throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to reversing the vertical velocity at the assigned altitude instead of leading it, did not complete the transition from climb to descent within the Vertical "S" pattern and did not re-establish the briefed rate. The A/C passed 400 feet beyond the reversal altitude and the rate diverged 500 feet per minute from the briefed value, with the result that the IP took the controls to re-establish the pattern. Further practice of the reversal lead point is required.

SP completed the Vertical "S" to the standard required for this section, but each reversal was initiated only after the IP's verbal reminder of the target altitude. The reversal altitudes were missed by 300 feet and the rate reached 300 feet per minute from the briefed value before the correction was applied. Marginal performance for the Training Section - unprompted anticipation of the reversal point is expected to improve.

SP flew consecutive Vertical "S" cycles without any verbal prompting from the IP, leading each reversal and re-establishing the briefed rate promptly. Errors were limited to 190 feet per minute on rate, 180 feet at the reversal and 12 knots on airspeed, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" accurately, promptly and with full competence, without mistakes and without the IP's intervention. The rate was maintained within 120 feet per minute, the reversals within 110 feet of the assigned altitudes, bank within 4 degrees and heading within 5 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" with exceptional accuracy, holding the briefed rate through each half-cycle and reversing without any interruption of the instrument cross-check. Deviations in rate, altitude, bank and airspeed were negligible and no correction produced an extreme or continuous attitude change. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not maintain the briefed rate through the turning half of the Vertical "S" and did not monitor the altimeter approaching the reversal. Bank diverged 15 degrees from the briefed value and the A/C passed 450 feet beyond the reversal altitude, with the result that the IP directed the correction and flew part of the following cycle. Distribution of the scan across the turn is required.

SP, due to an uncoordinated combination of pitch and bank at the reversal, did not hold the briefed rate while establishing the turn and induced continuous A/C attitude changes. Bank reached 10 degrees from the briefed value, the reversal was made 300 feet from the assigned altitude and airspeed reached 20 knots from the target. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal indications.

SP flew the Vertical "S" within the desired standards, initiating each reversal and holding the briefed bank without the IP's intervention. The rate twice reached 220 feet per minute from the briefed value and one reversal was made 200 feet from the assigned altitude, each corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent rate through the turning half of the pattern is expected to improve.

SP executed the Vertical "S" without mistakes and without the IP's intervention, with smooth and continuous control inputs through every reversal. The rate was held within 110 feet per minute, the reversals within 100 feet of the assigned altitudes, bank within 4 degrees and heading within 4 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Vertical "S" with exceptional accuracy, integrating rate, bank and airspeed control so that each cycle finished on altitude and on heading without a secondary correction. Deviations in rate, altitude, bank, heading and airspeed were negligible and the instrument cross-check was never interrupted. Above end of block MIF achieved.
